profile.summary: This is the in silico ligand-conditioned pocket design comparison published with TorchCraft. Ten chemically diverse small molecules, ALE, ATP, CHD, CMP, DLU, FAD, IAI, OQO, SAM and TRP, each serve as the ligand a design must build a pocket for. For each method and each ligand 500 designs are generated under that method's own default settings, and the two methods compared are BoltzDesign and TorchCraft. The paper states the 160-residue length and the absence of a supplied native scaffold for the TorchCraft designs. The designs are assessed in two ways: score distributions from AutoDock Vina and affinity predictions from Boltz-2, printed in Figure 5c and 5d, and separately a TorchScore pass rate for TorchCraft, where a design passes when its pLDDT exceeds 70 and its ipTM exceeds 0.7. Nothing here is measured experimentally.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Section 2.5 and Figures 5c and 5d; Appendix A.4.3.4; Supplementary Figures S8 and S9

summary_quotes.text: We evaluated a panel of ten small-molecule targets spanning different chemical structures, including nucleotides, cofactors, metabolites, and drug-like compounds (Supplementary Figure S8).[17, 20, 26, 27] TorchCraft generated 500 independent 160-residue proteins per ligand without a supplied native scaffold. Raw outputs were evaluated without post hoc sequence redesign or score-based preselection.

We evaluated the predicted ligand-binding proteins using AutoDock Vina scores and Boltz-2 affinity predictions (Figure 5c,d),[6, 28, 29] with TorchScore pass rates reported separately (Supplementary Figure S9). Score distributions varied across ligands and methods.

For TorchCraft, we additionally reported a TorchScore-based computational pass rate, where a design passed the computational criterion when TorchScore pLDDT exceeded 70 and TorchScore ipTM exceeded 0.7.

sections.title: What it measures
sections.body: Whether a design method can produce a protein that forms a plausible pocket around a specified small molecule, across a chemically varied panel. The ligands span nucleotides, cofactors, metabolites and drug-like compounds, so the panel also asks how the answer changes with ligand chemistry; the paper reports that score distributions varied across ligands and methods. Three different computational views are used rather than one: a physics-based docking score, a learned affinity prediction, and a predictor confidence pass rate.

sections.title: How it is built
sections.body: No dataset and no split. The panel is the ten ligands named in Supplementary Figure S8, chosen for chemical diversity. For each method and each ligand, 500 designs are generated with that method's default settings. For TorchCraft the paper adds that the designs are 160-residue proteins generated without a supplied native scaffold; Appendix A.4.3.4, which covers both methods, gives neither a length nor a scaffold condition for BoltzDesign. Raw outputs are evaluated without post hoc sequence redesign or score-based preselection. The design procedure that produced them is described in the appendix as a staged schedule in which the ligand is added and the interface objective is weighted up gradually, separating fold formation from pocket optimisation, but the benchmark itself is defined by the ligand panel, the design count and the three scores.

quotes.text: Figure S8 Small-molecule targets used in the SMI benchmark. Benchmark panel of chemically diverse ligand targets used for small-molecule interaction design, including ALE, ATP, CHD, CMP, DLU, FAD, IAI, OQO, SAM, and TRP.

We evaluated a panel of ten small-molecule targets spanning different chemical structures, including nucleotides, cofactors, metabolites, and drug-like compounds (Supplementary Figure S8).[17, 20, 26, 27] TorchCraft generated 500 independent 160-residue proteins per ligand without a supplied native scaffold. Raw outputs were evaluated without post hoc sequence redesign or score-based preselection.

For small-molecule binder design, we compared BoltzDe- sign and TorchCraft. For each method and each target, 500 designs were generated using the default settings of the corresponding method. BoltzDesign and the raw TorchCraft setting were evaluated without sequence redesign. The score distributions of the resulting designs were assessed with AutoDock Vina and Boltz-2. For TorchCraft, we additionally reported a TorchScore-based computational pass rate, where a design passed the computational criterion when TorchScore pLDDT exceeded 70 and TorchScore ipTM exceeded 0.7. We also tested a TorchCraft redesign variant in which ligand-interface residues were fixed, all remaining positions were redesigned eight times with LigandMPNN, and the redesigned sequences were refolded with TorchFold. The refolded structure with the highest pTM was selected as the redesigned structure and was then evaluated with AutoDock Vina and Boltz-2.

The ligand was then added, and the weight of the interface objective was gradually increased before the final optimization stages (Appendix A.1.3). This schedule separates initial fold formation from subsequent pocket optimization.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
sections.body: Two methods are compared, BoltzDesign and TorchCraft, and both are evaluated without sequence redesign in the arms that are compared directly. The score distributions of the resulting designs are assessed with AutoDock Vina and Boltz-2 and shown in Figures 5c and 5d. For TorchCraft alone, a TorchScore pass rate is also reported in Supplementary Figure S9: a design passes when TorchScore pLDDT exceeds 70 and TorchScore ipTM exceeds 0.7. A further TorchCraft variant is reported separately, in which ligand-interface residues are fixed, all other positions are redesigned eight times with LigandMPNN, the redesigned sequences are refolded with TorchFold, the structure with the highest pTM is kept, and that is then scored with AutoDock Vina and Boltz-2.

sections.title: What TorchScore is
sections.body: The scorer every pass rate in this panel depends on is worth stating plainly, because it is not an independent evaluator. TorchScore is a score-only loading of the same TorchFold implementation used for design: given input coordinates it skips the diffusion structure module and runs the confidence pathway, returning pLDDT, pTM and ipTM. No separate scoring network is trained, and in this study it used the pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights, the same checkpoint the designs were optimised against. Sequences rebuilt with FlowPacker are scored from those coordinates and are not refolded from sequence.

quotes.text: TorchScore is a score-only loading of the TorchFold implementation.[21] Given input coordinates, it bypasses the diffusion-based structure module and evaluates the complex through the confidence pathway, returning predictor-derived scores including pLDDT, pTM, and ipTM. No separate scoring network is trained.

In this study, TorchScore used pretrained AF3 weights, the same checkpoint used for design. Designed sequences that were rebuilt with FlowPacker were scored from the resulting coordinates; they were not refolded from sequence by TorchScore.

facts.label: Leakage controls
facts.value: None, and none is needed in the train and test sense: no model is trained here and the panel has no labels to hold out. What the sources do describe is a dependency that runs the other way, which the authors state plainly: TorchScore uses the same pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights that TorchCraft optimised against, so the scorer is not independent of the designer.

facts.value: None in this panel. Every criterion is computed by a predictor. The paper reports wet-lab binding measurements elsewhere in the study, for minibinders and VHHs against four targets each, but those campaigns are separate from this comparison.

facts.label: Adaptation
facts.value: No training or fine-tuning. Both methods run with their default settings, and TorchCraft optimises sequence logits through frozen pretrained AlphaFold 3 weights; the paper states that all designs reported in the study used pretrained AF3 weights. The only optional post-processing is the LigandMPNN redesign variant, which is reported as a separate arm.

notes: No numbers are printed for this panel: Figures 5c and 5d show Vina and Boltz-2 score distributions and Supplementary Figure S9 shows the TorchScore pass rates, so no result value is recorded. The structured size is the number of ligands, ten, as Supplementary Figure S8's caption names them; the 500 designs figure is per method per ligand, and the design length of 160 residues is a design setting, not a set size. The three structured entries are not all comparisons of two methods: the Vina and Boltz-2 distributions cover BoltzDesign and TorchCraft, while the TorchScore pass rate is reported for TorchCraft only. Metric direction is left null for the Vina and Boltz-2 entries because the paper reports them as distributions and does not state a direction for either score. The paper states no licence for itself; the code repository is Apache-2.0. The same paper is the source for four other records in this batch.
